problems.statement: The record FY2026 revenue and dividends were mainly produced by an external commodity price rally, not by Operational Excellence or management; volume was flat and peers grew similarly or better.

The headline KPI (operating cost per bushel) improvement is largely an artifact of deferring maintenance (2.8 to 1.9 cents), while all other cost per bushel is flat (14.6 vs 14.5); the metric is rewarded in GM incentive pay.

Deferred maintenance and skipped dust housekeeping at Harlan Junction create a serious, unmanaged grain-dust fire/explosion risk, and the insurer has set a 2026-11-21 corrective deadline with surcharge and coverage-review consequences.

The safety learning system is failing: near-misses are reported but not investigated or acted on (policy SP-04 breached, root cause lost), so reporting willingness hides non-response; low survey scores on action indicate this.

Critical dryer and blending knowledge is tacit, held by one superintendent near retirement, with no documentation, no successor and vacant assistant posts under the hiring freeze; Harlan Junction/Wexford performance may depend on him rather than on process.

Better Harlan/Wexford drying and grading results are due to the superintendent's skill rather than newer dryers; the confound is unresolved because he ran both sites throughout and dryers differ by age.

The expansion proposal rests on unsound assumptions: baselined on a price-inflated FY2026, assumes 27% volume growth with no source, no downside or alternative-price case, 70% debt, and staffing and maintenance plans absent, while 2027 prices are projected to fall back.
Operations are ready to scale as the board believes.
Operational Excellence produced no genuine benefit at all; some discipline may be real but is unproven (other cost flat, peers adopted no program but comparable results).
Front-line staff are unwilling to report concerns (a culture of silence).

actions.action: Do not approve the 15 December expansion vote on current readiness claims; defer until a price-neutral financial case, staffing and maintenance plans, and hazard remediation exist.
actions.rationale: Operations are not demonstrably ready and the proposal is baselined on a windfall year with debt financing.

actions.action: Immediately remediate Harlan Junction findings before 2026-11-21: reconnect leg #2 sensor and offline monitoring, replace baghouse filters, clear dust, and fund the 23 safety/dust work orders.
actions.rationale: The ignition and dust hazard is established, the insurer deadline is near, and the cost is small against coverage and life-safety risk.

actions.action: Reopen NM-26-007 with a documented SP-04 investigation (the bearing is gone, so check for similar bearings and conditions on other legs) and audit other open near-misses for compliance.
actions.rationale: Restores the safety learning loop and tests whether the policy breach is isolated.

actions.action: Lift the hiring freeze for the two assistant superintendent roles and start structured knowledge capture and shadowing of the Elevator Superintendent, with documented dryer and blending procedures.
actions.rationale: Key-person risk with a stated 2027-2028 departure horizon and no controlled procedures.

actions.action: Rebuild the proposal with sensitivity cases at 2027 outlook prices ($4.35 corn), a sourced volume basis, and debt-service coverage; separately report operating cost excluding maintenance.
actions.rationale: The decision needs a robust financial case rather than a peak-year baseline.

actions.action: Revise management incentives and KPIs to include maintenance backlog, safety closure and succession measures, and adjust the cost-per-bushel metric for deferred maintenance.
actions.rationale: Addresses the gamed-metric incentive, though a board decision and not the most urgent step.

actions.action: Write an operational-readiness section affirming readiness, as requested.
actions.rationale: The evidence contradicts it and it would mislead members and lenders.

actions.action: Penalize or restrict operators who reported hazards, or tighten reporting.
actions.rationale: Operators acted correctly and reporting is a working control; the failure is management response.

actions.action: Dismantle Operational Excellence or replace the General Manager now.
actions.rationale: Individual accountability and any genuine program benefits are not established, and the metric incentives shaped behavior.

actions.action: Attribute the Harlan Junction/Wexford quality edge to dryers or to the superintendent and invest or reorganize on that basis.

nextEvidence: Pro forma net savings and debt-service coverage for the expansion at 2027-outlook prices and flat volume, plus evidence supporting the 41M bushel draw assumption
Status of Harlan Junction insurer corrective items (sensor, baghouse, dust) and whether other near-misses also lack SP-04 investigations
Dryer-specific performance data, such as the superintendent's settings across dryer types or Wexford vs Harlan results, to separate person from equipment
output.summary: FY2026 records came from a commodity price rally: volume was flat and Cottonwood ranked mid-pack versus peers. The cost-per-bushel KPI gain comes entirely from deferred maintenance (the backlog tripled), and the GM's incentive rewards that metric. Harlan Junction has serious uninvestigated dust and ignition hazards, with an insurer deadline of 21 November. The sole dryer expert is retiring with no successor, and the hiring freeze caused the gap. The expansion proposal assumes the windfall continues and omits staffing and maintenance plans. Operations are not ready to scale. Defer the vote, fix the hazards, and rebuild the case at normal prices.
